messages:
sylvie: Quick FYI — saw a weird prod spike after the TF apply. Some model pods started reading old config keys. Anyone else?

dan: yeah saw that. seemed like the ConfigMap was rolled but pods still read the legacy key `models.default.features`. maybe shadowing?

priya: can you paste the pod logs or the cm yaml? my hunch is stale mount path or a different namespace.

 sylvie: logs: "WARN config: missing runtime_knobs.v2, falling back to default". Pod was `model-serve-redispatch-7f8c`. CM applied in `redwood-models` ns. Terraform change added `configmap.data["runtime_knobs.v2"]` but provider applied with replace instead of create_before_destroy.

jordan: if TF replaced the CM (delete+create) the volume mounts would be updated but kube may keep old mounted file until pod restart. that shouldn't change keys though; are we using projectedVolume with subPath? that can cause stale content.

priya: also check if we have two configmaps: `models-config` and `models-config-legacy`. maybe name collision after templating change. run: `kubectl get cm -n redwood-models -o jsonpath='{.items[*].metadata.name}'`

sylvie: ran that: output: models-config models-config-legacy models-config-202602. the tf module name got a suffix when replacing.

infra-bot: terraform-apply finished for workspace prod-models (plan #3127) — resources changed: 1 aws_ssm_param, 1 kubernetes_config_map (models-config -> models-config-202602).

dan: ok root cause: TF rename created a new CM and left consumers pointing to old one via mount references at release time. pods didn't restart, so they kept old content. short term: rolling restart for model deployments will pick new CM.

sylvie: rolling restart fixed the pods reading new keys. but we need a safer pattern. proposal: enforce `create_before_destroy = true` on configmap resource and pin `metadata.name = "models-config"` — or better, avoid destructive replaces by using non-destructive patching pattern in our infra module.

priya: agree. also add a CI lint that fails if a configmap resource lacks `lifecycle.create_before_destroy`. i'll add a terralint rule. open PR?

jordan: and add a terraform policy (opa) that rejects name-changing replacements for resources with label `models-config=true`. medium effort but prevents this class of bug.

sylvie: i'll open the PR to add lifecycle and a quick terralint check, pinging @priya for review.

dan: also let's add an annotation-based rollout helper so deployments auto-restart on config checksum change. we have a small controller that watches annotation `redwood.io/config-checksum` and restarts pods when it changes. add the annotation via k8s manifest/template.

priya: ack, will review after lunch.

sylvie: filing an incident note in postmortems later. :memo:

sylvie: code snippet i'll add to the module: 
```hcl
resource "kubernetes_config_map" "models" {
  metadata {
    name = "models-config"
    labels = { managed_by = "tf" }
  }
  data = {
    # runtime knobs, per-model overrides
  }
  lifecycle {
    create_before_destroy = true
  }
}
```

dan: nice. also add a comment in the module README about stable names and non-destructive updates. :thumbsup:

priya: thanks everyone, i'll review the PR and the terralint rule. if anyone wants to pair on the opa policy i can help this afternoon.

sylvie: thanks — will tag you in the PR when it's up.
thread_text: Quick thread about a TF-driven configmap rename causing pods to read stale config; rolled, fixed with restart, followups: add lifecycle.create_before_destroy, terralint check, OPA policy, and restart-annotation pattern.
